meta.title: Russian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 482 phrases · both directions, as two cards per phrase
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Russian → English and English → Russian, each a card with its own schedule. 482 Russian set phrases, idioms and proverbs — the layer a list of single words cannot carry, and the one thing the six TORFL level decks beside this one leave out (an expression one of them already teaches is not repeated here). The commonest come first: что это, не знаю, я не знаю, не думаю. WHAT COUNTS AS AN EXPRESSION is two tests, each catching what the other misses: an entry English Wiktionary files as a phrase or a proverb, or any entry of more than one word with a sense it marks as idiomatic — so ходи́ть вокру́г да о́коло, a verb, and головна́я боль, a noun, are both here. 75 of the entries are proverbs. Oaths and coarse expressions are left out. THE ORDER is how many sentences of the Tatoeba corpus use each expression, counted on whole words. 114 of the 482 appear in no sentence there at all, and they are kept and dealt last rather than dropped: an idiom is literary where a corpus of everyday sentence pairs is conversational, and letting the corpus choose would let it set the syllabus. Real example sentences come with 257 of the 482 expressions, three apiece for 125 of them. Every Russian word is printed with its stress mark; the sentences are printed as they were written. Sources. Expressions, meanings and stress: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order and example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
